learning_outcomes.text: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; choose and apply appropriately established analytical, computational and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial restrictions.

Ability to design, plan and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems in their specialty, which comply with established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Understanding of applicable techniques and analysis, design and research methods and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.
General ideas about economic, organizational and management issues (such as project management, risk and change management) in the industrial and business context.
Ability to collect and interpret data and manage complex concepts within their specialty, to make judgments that involve reflection on ethical and social issues.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to recognize the need for continuous self-training and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.
Ability to keep up to date with new developments in science and technology.
Define the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each one, and making correct use of language, in writing.

syllabus_topics: Project phase management: Monitoring and control
Project phase management: Completion and closure
Entrepreneurship: From Idea to Business Opportunity
teaching_methods: Development, drafting and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc., related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or control points
Teacher presentation in the classroom, in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Completion of exercises individually and in teams

assessment_methods.method: Technical ability, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation delivered, presentation and technical defense
Reports on exercises performed, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment and project feedback is provided. For the RGM330 competence, the subject work accounts for 70% and the semester project for 30%. For the RG301 competence, reports on exercises, case studies, computer/simulation/lab practices account for 50%, and technical ability, project involvement, work performed, results, documentation, presentation, and technical defense account for 50%. For the RGM329 competence, individual written and oral tests account for 80%, and reports on exercises, case studies, computer/simulation/lab practices account for 20%.
